title.narrative: Communication for Policy Research South : Favoriser l'émergence de décisionnaires pour améliorer les politiques
Communication for Policy Research South: Fostering Policy Leaders for Improved Evidence-based Policy in the Global South

description.narrative: This project will help develop a new wave of local network economy policy leaders across Asia and Africa. The network economy refers to the information society's emerging economic order, which is based on products and services created and accessed through social networks on a large scale. The project will equip policy leaders to engage in public interest research and support evidence-based network economy policy development and regulation. The goal is to establish and implement policies that help reduce poverty and support economic growth. While privately funded research in this area tends to focus on return on investment, the project's public interest research will concentrate on issues such as pro-poor access to information networks and protecting consumer rights. Communication regulatory structures in Africa and Asia are not designed to help reduce poverty and spur economic growth. The shortage of locally based policy and regulatory capacity is one of the reasons for this challenge. There are not enough people in place to effectively shape the policy agenda and regulations to achieve sustainable development objectives. This lack of capacity extends beyond government officials to civil society and academia. Building a local human resource base in different areas of the network economy sector is critical for the sector to develop and be sustainable. Compounding the problem is the lack of public-interest policy research to support evidence-based policy-making. The project aims to -stimulate local interest in public interest policy and regulatory research; -develop capacity to engage in public interest policy and regulatory research; and -contribute to the empirical knowledge base in the field of ICT policy and regulation to inform policy development and regulation in developing countries. The project team will undertake the following activities to achieve its objectives: -Support two annual regional policy conferences that will showcase public interest research on network economy policy and regulation in Africa and Asia; -Develop and deliver research training tutorials for young scholars; -Establish an internship program to support young scholars in Africa and Asia; and -Undertake evaluation activities to improve training for emerging policy leaders. The Communication for Policy Research South (CPRsouth) capacity building program is supporting the project. Two IDRC recipients, Lirneasia and Research ICT Africa (RIA), will lead it.
